appraisal_events.evidence: le corps d'un malade n'est plus qu'une cornue où s'observent des réactions chimiques... des petits points bleu de Prusse, qui avaient l'air de ne pas appartenir au monde vivant
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's description reduces Swann's dying body to an almost inhuman object of clinical observation, a stark diminishment that marks his nearness to death.

appraisal_events.evidence: Charlus... se garda bien de ne pas profiter [du moment]... un triomphal couplet dont la pauvre de Saint-Euverte, quasi immobilisée derrière nous, ne pouvait guère perdre un mot
appraisal_events.explanation: Physically trapped in the narrow alcove, Mme de Saint-Euverte cannot escape Charlus's mocking tirade; the narrator's sympathetic 'la pauvre' confirms the humiliation is real rather than merely her own perception.

status_effects.explanation: His body and face are rendered in dehumanizing, almost clinical terms that signal his advanced illness and approaching death.
She is publicly cornered and mocked by Charlus in front of Mme de Surgis, unable to escape or defend herself.
